subject: Oceanography
title: Seafloor Spreading
description: A quick win: understand Seafloor Spreading.

hook.text: In the 1960s, Harry Hess proposed that the ocean floor moves—it's created at ridges and destroyed at trenches.

buildup.text: Magma rises at mid-ocean ridges, solidifies into new crust, and pushes older crust outward.

discovery.text: Magnetic stripes on the seafloor proved it—lava records Earth's magnetic reversals as it solidifies.

twist.text: The oldest ocean floor is only 200 million years old—continents are 20 times older.

climax.text: Seafloor spreading confirmed drift and gave birth to the theory of plate tectonics.

punchline.text: The ocean floor is a conveyor belt—always being born and destroyed.

quiz.question: What evidence confirmed seafloor spreading?
options: Magnetic stripe patterns on the ocean floor
